newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mostly lower, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mostly lower, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle closed lower in nearby contracts with late commercial hedge selling featured in the actively-traded August, traders said.
Feeder cattle closed narrowly mixed after a thinly-traded session. Higher CBOT corn futures plus the late weakness in live cattle induced mainly local selling in nearby months.
Light feedlot sales this week created a bearish mood among some cattle traders, who said meat packers may try to lower bids next week to $64.00 per cwt versus this week's $65.00.
"I think everybody is looking for $64.00 next week," said one trader.
Not everyone agreed. After light cattle sales this week, some analysts and traders said meat packers will need cattle.
"I still think they will trade cattle at $65.00," said another analyst. "Unless the numbers come this afternoon, they (packers) will need cattle."
Higher CBOT corn prices and lower cash feeder prices prompted speculative selling in feeder cattle, traders said.
Late in the session, commercial interests were noted buying October and November feeder cattle and selling February 1998 and April 1998 live cattle.
Live cattle closed down 0.225 cent per lb to up 0.050 cent with June off the most at 65.125 cents. Feeder cattle were up 0.050 to down 0.250 cent with August unchanged at 78.325 cents.
